PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-05-11
57F, ambulatory visit for an annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. She reports mild ankle swelling by the end of the day over the past few weeks that improves overnight, prompting a cardiac screen today. Energy has been steady otherwise. Diet includes frequent sugary drinks, which was discussed. She works as a receptionist, mostly seated. Father with heart failure. Appetite is good and sleep is adequate. She takes her supplements as prescribed. Lives with her spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 124/78, HR 72, RR 14, Temp 98.1 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 166 lb, BMI 27.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
HEENT: normal.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur, no gallop.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: trace ankle edema, improves with elevation.
Labs (this week): Hgb 11.8 g/dL, A1c 6.0%, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, BNP 42 pg/mL, lipid panel within goal.

A/P:
1. R/o CHF; BNP normal. Ankle swelling is mild, improves overnight, and fits long hours seated at her desk; no echocardiogram needed. Advised leg elevation in the evenings and short walking breaks at work.
2. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks and adding regular walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
3. Anemia, stable on recheck. Continue oral iron daily with vitamin C. Repeat CBC in 3 months.
4. Family history: discussed father's history and reviewed warning signs to report. Confirmed age-appropriate screening is up to date.

Return in 3 months for routine follow-up, sooner for worsening swelling.
